links.outcome: Harmful content rates, purpose-built AI with layered safeguards vs general-purpose LLMs
links.effect: Harmful content lower for the purpose-built AI: suicide/NSSI .4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%; eating disorder 8.4% vs 54.0%; substance use 9.9% vs 45.0%.
links.quote: The purpose-built AI was significantly less likely than general-purpose LLMs to produce harmful content across suicide/NSSI (.4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%), eating disorder (8.4% vs 54.0%), and substance use (9.9% vs 45.0%) benchmarks.

links.outcome: Missed interventions for suicide risk and NSSI in real conversations
links.effect: Zero suicide-risk cases without crisis resources; 3 NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.
links.quote: Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.

links.outcome: Clinician review audit of real deployed conversations for safety estimation
links.effect: Clinician review of 20,000 real conversations found zero suicide-risk cases lacking crisis resources and identified NSSI false negatives. The authors conclude ecological audits are useful for estimating safety.
links.quote: Findings support the utility of ecological audits for safety estimation.
